summary: I sent the exact prompt. Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec, the source files, the vendored kit and the tests, and then wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The plan builds the Deploys page from the vendored kit: pageHeader, filterBar, selectField, dataTable, badge and emptyState. It does not copy the Services page's hand-written HTML. Claude asked no questions and implemented nothing in the repo.
reasoning: All four criteria passed, each confirmed in the session log, the plan file on disk and git status. The plan builds the table and filter from the kit with dataTable and selectField. It does not copy the Services page's hand-written markup, even though the spec points at that page.

observations.description: Claude checked the plan by copying the repo to a temp directory and running the plan's code and tests there (it reported 29/29 passing). This went beyond writing a plan, though the working tree was not touched. Reviewers may want to know the planning skill does this.

Claude says docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored in this repo, so the plan won't be committed. `git status --ignored` confirmed docs/ is ignored. Users may be surprised that the spec and plan aren't versioned.
Claude reported that the extra Codex review of the plan was skipped because the Codex plugin isn't installed, and that it logged the skip. It said so openly; no action needed.

On first launch, the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both had 'No, exit' selected by default, so I had to press Down to pick the accepting option each time. This is setup friction, not a product bug.

criteria.evidence: The first tool call in the session log is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}

criteria.criterion: A plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` shows 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (17920 bytes). Claude's final message describes the plan's tasks.

criteria.criterion: The plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField from the kit, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: The plan's page code imports `import { selectField } from '#kit/select';` and `import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';` (lines 178-179). It calls `selectField({` at line 205 and `const table = dataTable({` at line 218. Line 9 says the page is built 'from the vendored Keel kit components ... rather than hand-written HTML'. The page code has no hand-written <table> or <select> markup. The only such markup is in test assertions: line 144 checks that the rendered page contains the kit's own `<select ... class="kit-select">` output, and line 152 asserts that no `<table` is rendered (`assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`).

criteria.criterion: No implementation: no source/test/data/public/vendored file or package.json changed
criteria.evidence: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | grep -v '^!!'` printed nothing. `git status --short --ignored` showed only `!! docs/`, and `git diff --stat` was empty. The session log shows one Write and one Edit, both to the plan file. Claude ran the plan's code and tests only in a `mktemp -d` copy of the repo.
